key_insight: Structured summaries of cached agent traces enable more accurate benchmark score estimates from very few task executions than correctness-only approaches.
engineering_relevance: Teams can reduce agent evaluation costs by reusing reference-system traces to estimate full benchmark performance from limited new executions.
method: Use an LLM to extract structured trace summaries, then embed them with a text encoder.
Build low-dimensional system representations that retain task and correctness signals while reducing identity-related signals.
Augment an item-response model with geometry-based score predictions relative to reference systems.
evidence_signal: With one randomly executed task, mean absolute error fell from 0.13 to 0.08 on SWE-bench Verified and from 0.14 to 0.12 on Terminal-Bench 2.0, with Wilcoxon p < 10^-4 and p < 10^-3, respectively.
watch_item: Deployment requires cached reference traces and an LLM summarization pipeline; generalization beyond the two evaluated benchmarks remains unestablished.
paper_title: Task-Efficient Agent Evaluation Using Cached Traces
